llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed, read-only VMware Log Insight query helper, with local credential handling risks that users should manage carefully.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is centralized VMware log search, aggregation, metadata, and alert history, and the documented tools are read-only with no ingest, edit, or delete surface.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Usage is scoped to explicit VMware/vSphere/ESXi Log Insight contexts, with routing guidance away from unrelated vCenter alarms or performance metrics.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a uv package and Bash-accessible CLI commands, which is normal for this kind of tool but means users are trusting the package source as well as the skill text.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The network scope is described as the configured Log Insight appliance, TLS verification is on by default, and the setup guide says there are no webhook or unrelated outbound data flows.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill stores configuration locally, reads credentials from a chmod-600 .env file, rewrites plaintext passwords to base64 obfuscation, and records tool calls in a local audit database; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned but not strong secret protection.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing, use a read-only Log Insight service account, keep ~/.vmware-log-insight/.env chmod 600, and prefer injecting the password from a secret manager instead of leaving it in the .env file. Treat returned logs as sensitive operational data.
llm.findings: [RA2] expected: The local audit database and .env credential handling are real and disclosed in the artifact. Because the skill warns that base64 is only obfuscation, recommends secret-manager injection for real secrecy, and remains read-only, this is guidance-worthy rather than a Review-level concern.
